clue.text: Hit edges of hedgerow during approach

indicators.note: one piece sits during, so within, the other

parts.note: to tack is to approach on a slanting course, as a sailing boat does

indicators.note: only the outer letters, the first and last, of hedgerow are used

parts.note: first and last letters of hedgerow

explanation.surface: Someone strikes the sides of a hedge while walking up to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thwack is a sharp heavy blow, so the verb is a vivid synonym for striking.

clue.text: Word of advice: put on favourite scarf

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is put on top of the next

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone advises wearing their favourite scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippet is a long narrow scarf or cape worn round the shoulders, so it is a type of scarf.

clue.text: Fools adopting a billion animals

indicators.note: the fools take the letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: wallies is British slang for fools

explanation.surface: Foolish people take on a billion creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: A wally is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallabies are small Australian marsupials, an example of animals.

clue.text: Lowly worker grabs knight before a line dance

indicators.note: the letters so far come before the last piece
the worker grabs the knight, holding it inside

parts.note: a cog is a minor worker in a big machine

explanation.surface: A humble employee seizes a knight before a dance in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the chess notation for knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A conga is a dance performed in a long single-file line, so it is a line dance.

clue.text: Racing tip from Ascot — bet on it!

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Ascot is taken

parts.note: first letter of Ascot, the racecourse
a flutter is a small bet in British slang

explanation.surface: A tipster offers a racing tip for Ascot and urges you to back it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racing tip' reads as a horse to back; 'Racing' is actually the definition, as in a racing heart. A flutter is a modest wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that is racing with excitement or nerves is said to be all of a flutter, nervously excited.

clue.text: Picture that's been digitally rendered?

parts.note: digitally suggests computers, but it means done with the fingers, the digits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digitally' suggests computer graphics; a digit is also a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: This is artwork applied with the fingers rather than a brush, the digits being fingers.

clue.text: Driving in the city, perhaps, with not entirely sophisticated car

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, losing its last letter

parts.note: urbane means suave and sophisticated
the Golf is a Volkswagen car

explanation.surface: Someone drives round town in a rather unsophisticated car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' looks like motoring, but it is a golf drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban golf is a game played through city streets, so driving a ball in the city is an instance of it.

clue.text: Extremely tough mug for pound

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of tough
to mug is to rob

explanation.surface: A very hard mugging for a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat heavily and rhythmically, as the verb pound does.

clue.text: Warning: treadle right out of skew!

indicators.note: knocked askew, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An alert that a treadle is out of alignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of emergency warning.

clue.text: Savage gunfight was key in commemorative evening

indicators.note: a savage version of the words is mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brutal shootout was central to a night of remembrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November, marks the foiled 1605 plot to blow up Parliament, with bonfires and fireworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy Fawkes Night is an annual British evening marking the failed Gunpowder Plot, so it commemorates it.

clue.text: Friend, one of five picking up a final piece of ocean litter

indicators.note: the quintuplet picks up the earlier letters, following straight after them

parts.note: pal means friend

indicators.note: the final piece of a word is its last letter, here from ocean

parts.note: last letter of ocean
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A friend, one of quintuplets, collects rubbish from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish in the sea, but it is the old sense: a covered couch carried on poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A palanquin is a covered seat carried on poles by bearers, which is exactly a litter in the older sense.

clue.text: Dictator's committee dug deep?

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating aloud, so the word is as it would be spoken

parts.note: a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A tyrant's committee is pictured excavating a deep hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but it means one who dictates out loud, so the committee word is heard rather than read.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore is to drill a deep hole, so bored is a past-tense synonym for having dug deep.

clue.text: Sample from federal period

indicators.note: a sample is a small part taken out, so the answer lies inside federal

parts.note: the middle letters of federal spell the answer

explanation.surface: Someone takes a specimen from the federal period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long stretch of historical time, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fabled loner working to become chemist

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A legendary solitary figure gets to work and turns into a chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite and founded the Nobel Prizes.

clue.text: Dance introduces dated pieces that need arranging?

indicators.note: the dance comes first and leads into the next piece

parts.note: a jig is a lively folk dance
saw means dated, as in went out with someone

explanation.surface: A dance number brings in old-fashioned items that need sorting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' looks like old-fashioned, but it means courted; the question mark signals the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw puzzle consists of interlocking cut pieces that the solver must fit together correctly.

clue.text: What leaders of building industry near Dubai do to entrance?

parts.note: what the first letters do is spell a word

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what Dubai's builders do at the entrance to a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is the verb, to enchant, not a doorway; the question is answered by what the initials do.
explanation.definitionFit: To spellbind is to hold someone fascinated, so it is a synonym for the verb entrance.

clue.text: Idiot has cheap wine and beer regularly

parts.note: plonk is British slang for cheap wine

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one of beer

parts.note: second and fourth letters of beer

explanation.surface: A fool drinks cheap wine and has a beer now and again.
explanation.walkthrough: A plonker is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonker is mild British slang for a stupid person, a synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: King and queen with leader's headgear

parts.note: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher
a chief is a leader, and the possessive adds the s

explanation.surface: A king and queen along with the head's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerchiefs are cloths worn over the head, so they are a form of headgear.

clue.text: Follow up on unknown trouble with a movie

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the rest
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
Z is an unknown in algebra
ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: Someone pursues an unidentified problem with a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Godzilla is the Japanese monster film of 1954, later many remakes, so it is a movie.

clue.text: X-rated opening cut from mafia film excerpt

indicators.note: the opening, the first letter, of the phrase is cut off

parts.note: the mob is the mafia
a scene is a section of a film

explanation.surface: A violent gangster scene is trimmed for an adult-rated release.
explanation.walkthrough: A mob scene is also a crowded scene in a film; lose its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is indecent, the kind given an X rating, so the two match as adjectives.

clue.text: Case of importation business being weak

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so the first and last letters of importation

parts.note: first and last letters of importation
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: An import business is struggling and feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm describes someone frail or physically feeble, so it is a synonym for weak.

clue.text: Caught with speed? it's pure

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
haste means speed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something caught in a hurry can be pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually virtuous or innocent, close in sense to pure.

clue.text: Ocean swimmers not coming back on board after short race

indicators.note: the board piece comes after the cut-short word
the next piece goes on, so following, the board
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to zoom is to race along
a plank is a board

indicators.note: the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: Swimmers decline to return to the boat after a short race.
explanation.definitionFit: Zooplankton are tiny drifting animals in the sea, so they are swimmers in a loose, playful sense.

clue.text: Inception director may be found here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the beginning of something
second meaning: ..., where a film director works

explanation.surface: The film Inception's director is to be found here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inception' looks like the Christopher Nolan film, which ties in with director, but it is the plain noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset is the start of something; read as two words it is where a film director works.

clue.text: Name a sailor briefly associated with Hooters?

indicators.note: said briefly, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is linked by name to the Hooters restaurant chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter is slang for nose, so nasal means to do with noses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, and a hooter is slang for a nose.

clue.text: Come again, though only occasionally

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter of though is used

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of though

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a repeat, though rarely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations asking a speaker to repeat something not heard or understood.

clue.text: Girl hasn't finished drink

indicators.note: the word is left without its final letter

parts.note: lassie is a Scottish word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl has not finished her drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is a yogurt-based Indian beverage, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Made men stagger awkwardly carrying new spades

indicators.note: the shuffled word carries the other letters inside it
the letters of stagger are placed awkwardly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Men stumble clumsily while bearing fresh shovels.
explanation.walkthrough: A made man is a full initiated member of the Mafia. The shuffled word carries N inside, with S for spades closing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Made men are initiated mafiosi, so they are gangsters by definition.

clue.text: Medicine with smudged date on it

indicators.note: a smudged inscription is blurred, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medicine bottle has its expiry date smeared.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts poison, a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Palace in cathedral city diocese

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A palace sits within the diocese of a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee is the Paris palace that is the official residence of the French president.
